words_to_learn.definition_en: something, such as a task, that is assigned
words_to_learn.definition_vi: nhiệm vụ được giao, bài tập, chuyến công tác

examples.en: This assignment has to be turned in before midnight.
examples.vi: Bài viết/nhiệm vụ này phải được nộp trước nửa đêm.

examples.en: When the reporter is on assignment, research piles up on her desk.
examples.vi: Khi nữ phóng viên đi công tác viết bài, tài liệu nghiên cứu chất đống trên bàn làm việc của cô.

usage.tip: Cụm giới từ 'on assignment' (đang đi công tác/thực hiện nhiệm vụ được giao) là cụm từ cố định rất hay gặp.

extra_families.example: The chief editor assigned two veteran journalists to cover the trade summit.

words_to_learn.definition_en: to select one thing over another

examples.en: Alan chooses to read The New York Times over the Wall Street Journal.
examples.vi: Alan chọn đọc tờ The New York Times thay vì tờ Wall Street Journal.

examples.en: I did not choose that candidate to be the editor of our student newspaper.
examples.vi: Tôi đã không chọn ứng viên đó làm biên tập viên cho tờ báo sinh viên của chúng tôi.

word_family.example: No one was surprised when the student decided to choose a career in journalism.

collocations: have no choice but to V
usage.tip: Chú ý 3 dạng động từ bất quy tắc: choose - chose - chosen, và danh từ của nó là 'choice' (sự lựa chọn).

srs_sentence.en: Subscribers have the _____ of receiving the weekly magazine in print, digitally, or both.
srs_sentence.vi: Người đăng ký có quyền lựa chọn nhận tạp chí hàng tuần ở bản in, bản điện tử, hoặc cả hai.

words_to_learn.definition_vi: liên tục, luôn luôn, không ngừng

examples.en: An advantage of Internet news reports is that they can be constantly updated.
examples.vi: Một ưu điểm của các bản tin trên Internet là chúng có thể được cập nhật liên tục.

examples.en: People constantly look to the news to keep up-to-date on what is going on in the world.
examples.vi: Mọi người luôn tìm đến tin tức để cập nhật những gì đang diễn ra trên thế giới.

word_family.example: The reporter's constancy in writing thorough news reports earned her a loyal following of readers.
The constant ringing of the telephone distracted Susan from writing her report.
The editor constantly asks the reporters to recheck their facts.

usage.tip: Thường đứng giữa trợ động từ 'be' và V-ed/V-ing (is constantly updated / is constantly changing).

extra_families.example: Freelance journalists often struggle with an inconstant stream of income.

srs_sentence.en: In the digital age, newsrooms face _____ pressure to publish breaking stories immediately.
srs_sentence.vi: Trong kỷ nguyên số, các tòa soạn báo phải đối mặt với áp lực liên tục trong việc đăng tải tin nóng ngay lập tức.

words_to_learn.definition_en: to be the elements or parts of
words_to_learn.definition_vi: cấu thành, tạo thành, được coi là

examples.en: All the different news sources constitute the media industry.
examples.vi: Tất cả các nguồn tin tức khác nhau cấu thành nên ngành công nghiệp truyền thông.

examples.en: A talented staff, adequate printing facilities, and sufficient distribution points constitute a successful newspaper.
examples.vi: Đội ngũ nhân viên tài năng, cơ sở in ấn đầy đủ và các điểm phân phối rộng khắp tạo nên một tờ báo thành công.

structures: A, B, and C constitute + N
usage.tip: Là ngoại động từ (không dùng giới từ theo sau ở thể chủ động), thường mang nghĩa 'cấu thành/tạo nên' hoặc 'bị coi là vi phạm' (constitute a breach).

extra_families.example: Online subscriptions now constitute more than sixty percent of the paper's revenue.

srs_sentence.en: Advertising sales and digital subscriptions _____ the primary sources of income for the broadcaster.
srs_sentence.pos_hint: động từ chia hiện tại đơn số nhiều
srs_sentence.vi: Doanh thu quảng cáo và gói đăng ký kỹ thuật số cấu thành nguồn thu nhập chính cho đài phát thanh truyền hình.

examples.en: The court made the decision to allow the newspaper to print the controversial story.
examples.vi: Tòa án đã đưa ra phán quyết cho phép tờ báo đăng câu chuyện gây tranh cãi đó.

structures: make/reach a decision + to V / on N
usage.tip: Đi với động từ 'make' hoặc 'reach' (make/reach a decision); tính từ 'decisive' có nghĩa là 'quyết đoán' hoặc 'mang tính quyết định'.

extra_families.example: The managing editor acted decisively to retract the inaccurate article.

srs_sentence.en: Broadcast producers must be _____ when choosing which breaking news segment to air first.
srs_sentence.vi: Các nhà sản xuất chương trình phát sóng phải quyết đoán khi lựa chọn bản tin nóng nào sẽ lên sóng trước.

words_to_learn.definition_vi: phổ biến, truyền bá, phát tán (thông tin, tin tức)

part7.text: Questions 19–23 refer to the following two letters. April 12, 20— Michelle Richards News Story Weekly 346 Howard Avenue White River, NH Dear Ms. Richards, I am a journalist and an avid reader of News Story Weekly. It has long been my dream to write for your magazine. I graduated from National University a year ago with a degree in journalism. For the past six months I have been working as an investigative reporter for the Bluefield Daily, my hometown newspaper. This newspaper is disseminated throughout the state. I work on assignments involving local politics. In my opinion, News Story Weekly is the top news magazine in the country. It has had a great impact on my life. I started reading it at an early age, and it inspired me to pursue a career as a reporter. If there is a position available for a reporter at News Story Weekly, I would be interested in applying for it. I believe that my educational background and work experience qualify me for such a position. I am enclosing several of my articles that appeared in the Bluefield Daily as writing samples. I have letters of reference available if you need them. I look forward to hearing from you. Sincerely, Mark Conway April 19, 20— Mark Conway 1255 Park Place, Apt. 10 Bluefield, MA Dear Mr. Conway, Thank you for your letter of April 12 inquiring about a position as a reporter. We are constantly looking for reporters to work for our magazine, and we currently have an opening for a reporter to cover regional news. You seem to be well-qualified, and we would welcome your application. I would need to see your reference letters as well as a resume. The closing date for this position is May 15. We will make our choice after that date and let you know what we decide by the first of June. Thank you for your interest in News Story Weekly. Sincerely, Michelle Richards 22. ## Media

Study the following definitions and examples.

1. assignment n., something, such as a task, that is assigned

a. This assignment has to be turned in before midnight.

b. When the reporter is on assignment, research piles up on her desk.

2. choose v., to select one thing over another

a. Alan chooses to read The New York Times over the Wall Street Journal.

b. I did not choose that candidate to be the editor of our student newspaper.

3. constantly adv., continually

a. An advantage of Internet news reports is that they can be constantly updated.

b. People constantly look to the news to keep up-to-date on what is going on in the world.

4. constitute v., to be the elements or parts of

a. All the different news sources constitute the media industry.

b. A talented staff, adequate printing facilities, and sufficient distribution points constitute a successful newspaper.

5. decision n., judgment or choice

a. The court made the decision to allow the newspaper to print the controversial story.

b. Newspaper editors often have to make quick decisions about which stories to publish.

6. disseminate v., to scatter widely; to distribute

a. The media disseminates news across the world.

b. The computer virus was disseminated through the newsroom by reporters sharing terminals.

7. impact n., a strong, immediate impression

a. The story of the presidential scandal had a huge impact on the public.

b. The impact of the news coverage is yet to be known.

8. in-depth adj., in complete detail; thorough

a. The newspaper gave in-depth coverage of the tragic bombing.

b. Ivan's in-depth story on the spread of the disease received praise from many of his colleagues.

9. investigate v., to uncover and report hidden information a. Reporters need to thoroughly investigate the facts before publishing their stories.

b. Michelle's editor sent her to the capital to investigate the story behind the government scandal.

10. link n., an association; a relationship

a. The computer links will take you to today's headlines.

b. The father-daughter team of reporters is just one example of many family links at this newspaper.

11. subscribe v., to receive a periodical regularly on order

a. Jill subscribes to a gardening magazine.

b. It is convenient to subscribe to the newspaper because it is delivered to your house daily.

12. thorough adj., exhaustively complete

a. The reporters were thorough in their coverage of the event.

b. The story was the result of thorough research.

## Part 7 Reading Comprehension

Questions 19–23 refer to the following two letters.

April 12, 20—

Michelle Richards
News Story Weekly
346 Howard Avenue
White River, NH

Dear Ms. Richards,

I am a journalist and an avid reader of News Story Weekly. It has long been my dream to write for your magazine. I graduated from National University a year ago with a degree in journalism. For the past six months I have been working as an investigative reporter for the Bluefield Daily, my hometown newspaper. This newspaper is disseminated throughout the state. I work on assignments involving local politics.

In my opinion, News Story Weekly is the top news magazine in the country. It has had a great impact on my life. I started reading it at an early age, and it inspired me to pursue a career as a reporter. If there is a position available for a reporter at News Story Weekly, I would be interested in applying for it. I believe that my educational background and work experience qualify me for such a position. I am enclosing several of my articles that appeared in the Bluefield Daily as writing samples. I have letters of reference available if you need them. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

Mark Conway

April 19, 20—
Mark Conway
1255 Park Place, Apt. 10
Bluefield, MA

Dear Mr. Conway,

Thank you for your letter of April 12 inquiring about a position as a reporter. We are constantly looking for reporters to work for our magazine, and we currently have an opening for a reporter to cover regional news. You seem to be well-qualified, and we would welcome your application. I would need to see your reference letters as well as a resume. The closing date for this position is May 15. We will make our choice after that date and let you know what we decide by the first of June. Thank you for your interest in News Story Weekly.

Sincerely,

Michelle Richards
